author: bobyv87
text:
No problem. Thank you. I think i fond the answer anyway, last night.
So basically the scales are correlated in a way, between them. So, lets
 say we have a nice LS kink which is on h1 TF, if we really want to
trade it, we have to find which LS from LTF is correlated best with
HTF LS, so we look on the daily for larger LS which align with my h1
LS. In this way we can find running trades, and that can stop us from
trading in the middle. Another way it could be to follow FLs. Lets say a
 HTF FL breaks, so price can retrace to the next FL in the same HTF
scale before it can hit the target. In this way, any of lower TF FLs
are just middle levels. Of course, i can wait for first piece of PA to
occur (in much lower TF) and after that i have again a new scale to
work with, but i can't expect the whole HTF space to be filled, as a
reaction to an LTF FL.

author: Frosty
text:
I got two similar guidance regarding scales today. One from HCDE and one from Boby:

HCDE: I think the weight of thing is linked to what we see on
chart, i mean if a LS is seen on M10 and not on H4, then it's kink is of
 no importance. But if that m10 ls KINK is aligned with a H4 LS, and has
 clean orders, it can be of vital importance. That's how i try to assess
 targets too, i ask myself: what LS are we reacting to? Is this a target
 and on what scale? is there order flow where we are reacting? If no,
isn't it, in some way, an engulf giving indications for the next moves?
Where is the origin of the move that brought us there?

Boby: So basically the scales are correlated in a way, between
 them. So, lets say we have a nice LS kink which is on h1 TF, if we
really want to trade it, we have to find which LS from LTF is correlated
 best with HTF LS, so we look on the daily for larger LS which align
with my h1 LS. In this way we can find running trades, and that can stop
 us from trading in the middle. Another way it could be to follow FLs.
Lets say a HTF FL breaks, so price can retrace to the next FL in the
same HTF scale before it can hit the target. In this way, any of lower
TF FLs are just middle levels. Of course, i can wait for first piece of
PA to occur (in much lower TF) and after that i have again a new scale
to work with, but i can't expect the whole HTF space to be filled, as a
reaction to an LTF FL.

Then one important hint from bro Staurum: On another issue, here is what i have on my trading plan: Look out for unvisited zone for:

Generally, unvisited zone marks a higher scale trade, and therefore
higher win/loss ratio + higher R. However, its rarity is what patience
must fight for.

Visited zone, on the other hand, marks a lower scale trade and is easily
 FO-ed by the higher scale PA. Not as high win/loss ratio + not as high R
 must be within expectation because the trades are not so rare and
therefore patience required is not as intense.

I feel by thinking about the guides above and practicing into the charts, we will understand about scales eventually.

Please correct me if I'm wrong, IF and seniors

I appreciate all of your guidance and comments
